interpretations: Filter `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99 (so 21.99 and above), compute per-rating AVG(length) and per-rating AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) over individual films, then return one row with the plain average of the per-rating lengths and the plain average of the per-rating ratios (macro average of group averages, each rating weighted equally), unrounded.
Same as above, but the filter is greater than or equal to 20.99 (including films costing exactly 20.99).
Per-rating ratio is the average of each film's own rental_rate / replacement_cost; the final ratio is the average of those per-rating averages.
Per-rating ratio is AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(replacement_cost) within the rating (ratio of averages); the final ratio is the average of those per-rating values.

Missing values are ignored independently per measure: NULL lengths are skipped in the length average, and NULL ratios are skipped in the ratio average, so each average may use a different set of films.
Films with a missing length or a missing ratio are dropped from both per-rating averages, so both use the same set of films.
Ratings with no film above the cost threshold are omitted from the final average (not counted as zero).
A NULL rating, if present, is treated as its own group and included in the average of per-rating averages.
Films with a NULL rating are excluded, so only the five defined ratings are averaged.
Result is one row with two columns: average of per-rating average lengths first, average of per-rating average ratios second.
The final averages are weighted by the number of qualifying films per rating, which gives the overall film-level averages instead of the average of the group averages.
Films are weighted by their inventory copies (via the inventory table) rather than counted once each when computing the per-rating averages.
Ratio of sums per rating: SUM(rental_rate) / SUM(replacement_cost), with the final ratio the average of those per-rating values.
Ratings with no film above the cost threshold are kept in the final average as zero.
